_doc: Studio service bench, video slot: POST /api/services/video with a license token drives the full path — AuthMiddleware -> license gate -> slot resolution (byo_mode honoured) -> AIContentGenerationClient list/submit/poll -> MinIO store -> service_runs row. Added 2026-11-02 because it was the one slot with no live evidence at all. `seconds: 1` keeps the render at its floor; the route's own budget is 300 s (routes/service_lab.py::_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), so the probe asks for 360.

body.prompt: a single lit candle on a dark table, slow push-in

_expect_doc: 200 is the honest expectation on this deployment: ACG registers the `stub` renderer (VIDEO_PROVIDER=stub), which returns a placeholder clip — the bench's own page labels it `result-stub`, so a stub answer is a real answer here, not a silent fake. If this scenario ever returns 409 `provider_unavailable`, that means the deployment has NO registered video provider at all: report it as a configuration finding and re-point this scenario at the 409 shape — do not paper over it with a permissive assertion.
_wire_doc: Field names are snake_case on the wire (`created_at`, `media_url`, `output_kind`): `ServiceRunView` sets `model_config = _camel`, but that ConfigDict has no alias_generator, so the name is a misnomer. Same trap the image scenario documents at length.
_cost_doc: Kept `nightly: false` + `rotation: false`: a video render is the most expensive bench call and this is proof of a shipped feature, not a per-night regression.
